name: Natural Rhythm Cut
use_when: The goal is invisible editing or natural flow.
A shot contains physical action, walking, dialogue rhythm, or environmental cycles.
The current cut feels technically correct but rhythmically early or late.
Waveform-based trimming has made a human story feel disrupted or too mechanical.
avoid_when: The desired emotion is discomfort, shock, agitation, or interruption.
The edit needs a deliberate pattern break.
Following the rhythm would hide an important story point.

timeline_pattern.review: Loop the shot until the cut point feels apparent, then watch cold to verify.
timeline_pattern.waveform_warning: Use waveforms to find candidates, but choose the final cut by visual rhythm, breath, face, and story.

motion.rule: Match added motion to the source rhythm instead of fighting it.

sound.rule: Use speech cadence, footsteps, impacts, and ambience to locate natural cut points.
sound.avoid: Audio pops or abrupt ambience changes that make invisible cuts visible.

captions.rule: Caption changes should respect speech rhythm and not lag behind the cut.

color.rule: Shot matching should support invisibility; avoid grade jumps at rhythm cuts.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use timeline contact sheets and waveforms around candidate cut points. Add short audio fades at cuts to preserve natural rhythm.
implementation.remotion: Use frame markers for action completion, breath, or line ending; align sequence boundaries to those frames.
implementation.blender: Match camera or graphic motion to the cadence of the source footage.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Split on action completion, breath, or line cadence; use simple cuts unless the rhythm asks for a transition.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use trim mode and loop playback around the edit point to feel whether the cut lands naturally.

common_mistakes: Cutting only by transcript text and ignoring visual rhythm.
Cutting everything by waveform so the edit loses human continuity.
Cutting before a gesture or breath resolves.
Adding transitions that break an otherwise invisible cut.
Ignoring ambience changes at the edit point.
qc: Does the cut disappear when watched at normal speed?
Does the motion or speech cadence feel complete enough before the cut?
Is the audio bed smooth across the boundary?
Would a viewer notice the cut for the wrong reason?
Did waveform trimming preserve the human rhythm of the line or interaction?
